title: Independent ACIS reader alternatives and peer-writer state
mode: Deeper/broader primary-source research and plan update
scope: Broaden the direct SAT/SAB semantic-reader search beyond open-source codec projects
Separate candidate external geometry evidence from open-source support and kernel-independence claims
Refresh FreeCAD's current ACIS-consumer boundary and ACadSharp issue/PR state
Refine existing PAR-07/S7/S8 gates without changing implementation order or validation cadence

sources.project: Ansys CAD Integration ACIS reader, Release 2025 R2
sources.observation: The vendor documents a direct SAT/SAB reader configured during Ansys installation, operating in reader mode, for ACIS input versions R1-2023 on Windows and Linux. It imports solid, surface, and line bodies and transfers units when encoded. The page does not identify parser/kernel lineage or provide a stable programmatic geometry-extraction contract; it excludes non-commercial, education, alpha, beta, and PR builds from supported versions. This is an optional commercial semantic-reader candidate, not an admitted independent vote.

sources.project: FreeCAD Draft DXF and DWG import documentation
sources.observation: The current DXF guide distinguishes built-in C++ and optional legacy Python importers and states embedded binary ACIS/SAT solids cannot currently be read. The DWG route converts through an external converter before the selected DXF importer, so native converter success and ACIS semantic acceptance remain separate.

ACIS SAT/SAB read/write is a commercial component that translates through OCCT shapes/XDE and documents configurable healing and approximation. It is not part of the standard open-source OCCT format set and shares the OCCT kernel family with FreeCAD Part and CadQuery/cq-acis.

The reviewed sources describe bounded rather than general independent semantic evidence: ezdxf supports a limited ACIS subset and flat-face projection; cq-acis is experimental and uses OCCT conversion; ACadRust advertises a separate SAT/SAB topology model but its release and self-tests do not supply independent geometry truth; CADKernel's detailed matrix marks ACIS SAT/SAB read/write unimplemented. This screen is not exhaustive and does not prove no other open-source reader exists.

sources.project: ACadSharp ACIS writer issue and PRs
sources.observation: The issue #1195 and PRs #1150, #1240, and #1174 are open on the reviewed pages. #1150 discusses separate legacy-inline, modern DXF ACDSDATA, pre-2013 DWG-inline, and modern DWG AcDs routes and contributor-reported native/ODA opens. The thread also reports post-schema-refactor group-310 readback loss and conflicts with the evolving DWG reader; these are branch-specific reports, not a released/current-master result.

existingSubplansRefined: PAR-07/S7/S8: add Ansys only as a one-time, license-gated external SAT/SAB semantic-reader candidate whose implementation lineage and geometry extraction must be qualified first
PAR-07/S8: keep direct SAT/SAB semantics separate from DWG AcDs or DXF ACDSDATA owner/key closure and from FreeCAD acceptance
External peer ledger: keep ACadSharp open PR branches out of released capability claims and bind future inspection to exact base/head/source identity
assessment.planImpact: Add one optional, license-gated Ansys SAT/SAB route for future semantic cross-check only after lineage and machine-readable geometry extraction are established. It cannot by itself qualify outer DWG/DXF carriers, owner/key joins, FreeCAD behavior, open-source support, or any deferred J item.

method.limitations: The Ansys page is vendor product documentation and does not identify parser/kernel lineage, a scriptable geometry extraction route, or the license entitlement available to this repository owner. The open-source search is not exhaustive. Current GitHub issue and pull-request text is peer-maintained, branch-specific evidence. No runtime, license, or sample was used.
